result_text:
I fixed the bug in `isort/core.py`. Running the issue's example with `--sort-reexports` now gives sensible output. The imports are reformatted and `__all__` becomes `('func1', 'func2')`, with no leftover fragments.

The old code tracked where the `__all__` block starts in the output by adding up the lengths of the input lines it had seen. That drifted whenever the import section was rewritten (multi-line imports collapsed, comments at the top of the file), so the sorted `__all__` was written at the wrong offset and overwrote part of the imports.

The code now flags the `__all__` line when it sees it. After that line is written to the output, it sets the start position from `output_stream.tell()` minus the line's length, so the position is correct whatever the imports before it did to the output.

I checked it on a trimmed copy of the issue's file (two imports and two names instead of four). `tests/unit/test_isort.py` and `tests/unit/test_regressions.py` pass: 285 passed, 1 skipped. I didn't add a test, as you asked. My attempt to run a wider set with `-k` failed with 8 errors collecting the test files, so I didn't run the rest of the suite.
